evals.prompt: Bikin landing page untuk app invoice tracker. Target user freelancer Indonesia. Harus ada hero section, fitur highlights (3 fitur utama), pricing section (free dan pro), sama footer. Pake Next.js + Tailwind. Jangan yang generic startup template ya, buat yang beda.
evals.expected_output: Should produce a design system first (colors, typography, spacing tokens), then build components consuming those tokens. Should NOT use default blue/purple SaaS colors. Should have a distinctive visual identity. Design system should use 3-level token architecture (raw > semantic > component). Should include animation tokens. Layout should use asymmetry or visual tension, not centered-everything.
expectations: Output defines a design system with CSS variables or Tailwind config BEFORE component code
Color palette is NOT the default blue-purple-white AI aesthetic (no #6366f1, #8b5cf6, or similar)
Typography uses a non-default font pairing, not just Inter/system-ui
Components reference design tokens, not hard-coded color values
Hero section has a specific visual treatment beyond just centered text on a solid background
No sentences like 'modern, scalable landing page' in comments or documentation
Responsive strategy is addressed (mobile layout differs from desktop, not just shrunk)
Design system includes animation/transition tokens (timing functions, durations) as named values, not ad-hoc inline values
Token architecture has at least 2 levels: raw/primitive values and semantic aliases (e.g. --blue-600 mapped to --primary, not just flat color names)
At least one layout section uses asymmetry, offset, overlap, or broken grid — not all sections are symmetrically centered

evals.prompt: I need a dashboard UI for a project management tool. Show: task list with status columns (kanban style), a sidebar with project navigation, and a top bar with user avatar and notifications. Use React + any CSS approach. Make it look premium, not like a Jira clone.
evals.expected_output: Should create a distinctive dashboard that doesn't look like every other kanban board. Design system first with 3-level tokens. Should address interaction states (hover, drag, empty states) across ALL components not just buttons. Should have visual personality. Should include skeleton/loading states.
expectations: Design system tokens are defined before any component code
Kanban columns have visual differentiation beyond just text labels (colors, icons, or visual weight)
Sidebar has hover/active states defined, not just static layout
Empty state is addressed (what does an empty column look like?)
Shadow, border-radius, or gradient values come from the design system, not inline
Output does NOT look like a Bootstrap/Material UI default theme
Animation or transition is used for at least one interaction (drag, hover, or navigation)
Loading/skeleton state is defined for at least one data-dependent component (task cards, project list, or notification panel)
Focus-visible styles exist on interactive elements (keyboard accessibility) — not just hover states
Design rationale is present: at least one comment or doc section explaining WHY specific colors, spacing, or visual choices were made

evals.prompt: Redesign this login page. Currently it's just a white page with a centered card, email/password inputs, and a blue login button. Make it look like a premium fintech app. Vue 3 + CSS, no Tailwind.
evals.expected_output: Should transform a generic login into something with visual identity. Should use CSS custom properties with semantic naming (not just --color-1). Should consider ALL states (loading, error, success, disabled). Should have depth/atmosphere beyond flat white. Should verify CSS feature support is current.
expectations: Background is NOT plain white — uses gradient, pattern, image, or dark theme
CSS custom properties (--var) are used for colors and spacing, not hard-coded values
Login button has distinct hover, focus, and loading states
Error state is visually designed (not just red text under input)
Form inputs have custom styling beyond browser defaults
Uses CSS animations for at least one element (entry animation, loading spinner, or transition)
Output includes focus-visible styles for keyboard accessibility
CSS custom properties use semantic names (--primary, --surface, --error) not raw names (--color-1, --blue, --dark-bg)
Success state after login is visually designed (not just a redirect — shows confirmation feedback)
Disabled state for submit button is visually distinct from default state (not just opacity change)
